hook: The $299 robot mop isn't $299. Here's the real yearly cost.

scenes.visual_prompt: Price tag reading $299 on a robot vacuum box, camera pulls back to reveal a stack of replacement parts boxes next to it
scenes.voiceover: The $299 sticker price doesn't cover the full first year of owning this thing.

scenes.visual_prompt: Close-up of worn, frayed robot vacuum mop pads next to a fresh replacement pair
scenes.voiceover: Replacement mop pads typically wear out in three to six months, depending on your floor.

scenes.visual_prompt: Dustbin bag being pulled out and tied off like a kitchen trash bag, drawstring visibly straining
scenes.on_screen_text: Dustbin bags: same cadence as kitchen trash
scenes.voiceover: The dustbin bag needs a liner swap on the same cadence as your kitchen trash can.

scenes.visual_prompt: Drawstring trash bag failing and spilling dust, then a tear-resistant bag holding firm side by side
scenes.on_screen_text: $13.32 for bags that don't rip mid-swap
scenes.voiceover: Cheap liners split under fine dust — a tear-resistant pack runs about thirteen dollars and solves that.

scenes.visual_prompt: Calculator graphic adding up $15-20 next to a quarterly calendar
scenes.voiceover: Budget an extra fifteen to twenty dollars a quarter for bags, pads, and dock-cleaning solution.

scenes.visual_prompt: Robot vacuum's low-bag indicator light blinking red on the dock display
scenes.on_screen_text: Don't find out at the low-bag light
scenes.voiceover: That's a better time to learn this than when the low-bag indicator lights up in month two.

scenes.visual_prompt: Clean kitchen floor, robot docked quietly, text overlay with link icon
scenes.on_screen_text: Full consumables list on the blog
scenes.voiceover: I listed every consumable and the price on each — link's in my bio.

caption: Nobody mentions the consumables when they post the $299 price. I did the math on mop pads, dustbin bags, and dock solution so you're not surprised in month two. Full cost breakdown linked in bio.
